title: Morning Tea
content:
Steam climbs slowly from the cup,
the kettle hums its quiet tune.
The window frames a waking street
that will be loud and busy soon.

I hold the warmth between my hands
and let the minutes drift away.
Before the world begins to ask,
this cup is all I need today.

title: The Lighthouse Keeper
content:
He climbs the stairs at half past eight,
the lamp is waiting at the top.
The sea below is never still,
the waves forget the way to stop.

He trims the wick and cleans the glass,
he counts the ships that pass at night.
No one will know his name at dawn,
but every sailor knows his light.

title: Paper Boats
content:
We folded boats from yesterday's news
and set them down where the gutter ran.
They sailed past stones like distant isles
as only paper vessels can.

Some of them sank by the corner store,
some of them vanished into the drain.
We never learned where the brave ones went,
but we folded more when it rained again.

title: Autumn Ledger
content:
The maple keeps a careful book
of every leaf it lends the ground.
It writes in red, it writes in gold,
and never makes a single sound.

In spring it will collect its debts
in buds as green as they are small.
The tree is patient with the year;
it knows that nothing's lost at all.

title: Small Hours
content:
The clock is louder after two,
the fridge begins its midnight song.
The house is thinking its own thoughts
the way it has done all along.

I lie awake and listen close
to floorboards settling into place.
The dark is not a frightening thing,
just daylight with a quieter face.

title: Train Window
content:
Fields go by like turning pages,
fences stitch the hills together.
A horse looks up and then looks down,
unbothered by the passing weather.

I do not know the towns we cross,
their names are gone before I read.
But every station waves at me
as if it knew the life I lead.

title: The Gardener
content:
She kneels beside the tomato vines
and talks to them in a whispered tone.
She tells them news about the town,
she tells them they are not alone.

The neighbours smile and shake their heads,
but every summer, row on row,
her garden is the greenest one,
and only she and the plants know.

title: Snow Day
content:
The schools are closed, the roads are white,
the buses rest beneath their sheets.
The children own the world today
and build their castles in the streets.

By evening all the gloves are wet,
the cocoa steams on every sill.
Tomorrow it will melt away,
but no one minds; the day stands still.

title: Old Bicycle
content:
It leans against the garden shed,
its chain a little red with rust.
It carried me to school and back
and never once betrayed my trust.

I oil the gears, I pump the tyres,
I wipe the saddle clean of dust.
We ride again along the lane
because, it seems, we really must.

title: Harbour Market
content:
The fishmongers are shouting prices,
the gulls are circling overhead.
A woman sells a basket of lemons,
a baker sells his morning bread.

By noon the stalls are packed away,
the cobblestones are rinsed and bare.
Only the smell of salt remains
to prove the market ever was there.

title: Letters
content:
I found a box of letters once
tied up with string beneath the stair.
The ink had faded into brown,
the paper smelled of someone's hair.

I did not read them, not a line;
I tied the string and closed the lid.
Some stories should be left alone
to keep the secrets that they hid.

title: Lantern Walk
content:
We carried lanterns through the park,
a line of small and swaying stars.
The grown-ups talked of grown-up things,
of taxes, weather, broken cars.

But we were sailors in the dark,
explorers on a lantern sea,
and every shadow by the pond
was just as brave as we could be.
